set_aside.subject: AuditRecord occurred_at ownership
set_aside.text: “audit_writer supplies audit_id and occurred_at; callers cannot supply either” conflicts with “Each operation reads the clock once ... and that one instant supplies every portal-owned timestamp it writes” when the owning use case also writes business timestamps.
set_aside.question: Who reads the operation’s single clock instant, and how does audit_writer receive or share it without the caller supplying occurred_at?
options: The owning use case reads the clock once and passes the instant separately from AuditIntent to audit_writer.
audit_writer reads the clock once and returns or exposes that instant for all other records written by the operation.
A transaction-scoped clock context supplies the same instant to both modules.
set_aside.default_guess: Let the owning use case read once and pass the instant as a separate append_audit argument, while audit_writer constructs the AuditRecord.

witness.initial: An active project has an inactive budget version ready for activation.
events: budget_management writes activated_at and deactivated_at for the budget records.
outcomes: Following A28, all business and audit timestamps are the same operation instant.
Following the statement that audit_writer supplies occurred_at independently, audit_writer reads time separately and the audit timestamp can differ from the activation timestamps.
witness.observer: A staff member or investigator comparing the budget-version and audit records.

set_aside.subject: Audit entity identifier validation
set_aside.text: A23 requires rejecting “another entity's identifier”, while audit_writer knows only models, receives only AuditIntent, and “Must not own ... action-specific details”; the owning use case itself chooses entity_id.
set_aside.question: Which module owns verification that entity_id identifies the entity actually affected, rather than merely being a canonical UUID string?
options: The owning use case owns semantic binding; audit_writer validates only canonical syntax and presence rules.
audit_writer receives additional trusted evidence identifying the affected entity and validates equality.
The repository or transaction context verifies the referenced entity.
set_aside.default_guess: Make the owning use case responsible for semantic binding and limit audit_writer to canonical-form and action-shape validation.

witness.initial: Expenses A and B exist in the same project.
events: expense_management commits the correction but constructs an AuditIntent whose canonical entity_id is Expense B's UUID.
outcomes: audit_writer accepts the syntactically canonical UUID, leaving the audit history saying Expense B was corrected.
audit_writer detects the mismatch and rejects the append, causing the correction transaction to roll back.
witness.observer: An administrator or investigator reading the audit history.

set_aside.subject: Actor provenance for failed staff login
set_aside.text: A13 requires staff.login_failed records, but M36 requires actor_id unless actor_kind is system, and an existence-hiding failed login may not resolve any StaffAccount.
set_aside.question: What actor_kind and actor_id must audit_writer record for staff.login_failed when the submitted email is unknown, and must known-account and unknown-account failures be indistinguishable in audit?
options: Record every failed login as system with no actor_id.
Record a resolved staff_id for known accounts and system/no actor for unknown accounts.
Use another explicitly defined non-principal actor representation for every failed login.
set_aside.default_guess: Record every failed login as system with no actor_id so audit records do not reveal account existence.

witness.initial: Staff account alice@example.com exists; no account exists for bob@example.com.
events: A caller attempts login for alice@example.com with a wrong password.
The caller then attempts login for bob@example.com with any password.
staff_identity asks audit_writer to append staff.login_failed for both attempts.
outcomes: Both records use system/no actor_id, so the audit representation does not distinguish whether the email exists.
The Alice failure names Alice's staff_id while the Bob failure uses system/no actor_id, revealing account existence to an audit reader.
witness.observer: Any administrator or operator able to inspect audit records.
